findings.finding: Zabhlrsc extension ID is absent from the riscv_isa_ext_id enum. Integration requires adding a new ID (e.g., 106 or next available) alongside existing ZABHA (ID 90) and ZALRSC (ID 98). If a PR adds this without allocating a proper extension ID, hwprobe, KVM, and cpufeature dispatch will silently fail to recognize the extension, causing function_loss: userspace sees no Zabhlrsc support even when hardware has it.
findings.snippet:
#define RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZABHA		90
...
#define RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZALRSC		98
#define RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZICFISS		105
/* Zabhlrsc ID would go here but is missing */

findings.finding: ZALRSC is listed as a dependency of 'A' in riscv_a_exts[], but Zabhlrsc (byte/halfword LR/SC) is not present. If Zabhlrsc is integrated, it should be considered whether it is a sub-extension of A or ZALRSC, or an independent optional extension. Missing this dependency chain means the kernel may advertise 'A' compliance without Zabhlrsc support, yet CHERI requires Zabhlrsc. This creates a semantic gap where CHERI-capable hardware would appear to support 'A' but lack byte/halfword LR/SC needed for capability atomics.

The masked xchg fallback for byte and halfword sizes uses lr.w/sc.w with masking (lines 32-53), emulating byte/halfword atomics within word-aligned bounds. Zabhlrsc provides native lr.b/lr.h and sc.b/sc.h, which would eliminate the need for this masking emulation and provide better forward-progress guarantees. If Zabhlrsc is integrated but the alternative dispatch in cmpxchg.h is updated incorrectly (e.g., the ZABHA-only fast path at lines 22-30 is expanded for Zabhlrsc without proper ordering wrt fences), it could introduce subtle memory ordering bugs in capability atomic operations on CHERI hardware.

KVM ISA extension allowlist includes ZABHA and ZALRSC but no Zabhlrsc entry. If a guest tries to use Zabhlrsc, KVM must either trap-and-emulate or pass through the extension. Without Zabhlrsc in the KVM allowlist, guests cannot discover or use byte/halfword LR/SC, which CHERI guests would require for capability atomics. This is a virtualization gap: function_loss for CHERI VMs.

ZABHA has a boot-time setup check (enable/disable ELF hwcap) and a Kconfig TOOLCHAIN_HAS_ZABHA gate. Zabhlrsc would need a similar TOOLCHAIN_HAS_ZABHLRSC Kconfig entry plus a setup.c ELF hwcap enablement block. Without this, CHERI-aware userspace cannot detect Zabhlrsc via hwcap/ELF, causing function_loss for CHERI userspace that needs byte/halfword capability atomics.
findings.snippet:
if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZABHA) &&
    ...
    riscv_isa_extension_available(NULL, ZABHA) &&
    ...)
/* Zabhlrsc equivalent check is missing */
